Un citoyen français détenu par l'ICE aux États-Unis: sa femme raconte son calvaire à RFI

articles.summary: L’agence Reuters puis NBC News ont avancé que le cloud de l’armée de l’air avait été piraté, exposant possiblement « des informations militaires sensibles ».

articles.title: Trump’s Embrace of Xi and Huang Stuns China Critics in Washington
articles.summary: Warnings from hard-liners have grown more urgent amid what some call a winner-take-all race for A.I. dominance.

articles.title: Au Canada, le premier ministre, Mark Carney, promet la fin du sans-abrisme d’ici à dix ans
articles.summary: Le gouvernement s’est engagé à éradiquer un phénomène qui touche de plus en plus de Canadiens. Un défi de taille dans un pays victime d’une sévère crise du logement. A Montréal, le loyer moyen a augmenté de près de 70 % en moins de dix ans.

articles.title: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, New York’s First Female Senate Majority Leader, Dies
articles.summary: Ms. Stewart-Cousins, 76, served in the State Senate for 20 years. Her sudden death leaves a leadership void among top state Democrats.

articles.title: 2 American Airlines Jets Clip Wings at Reagan Airport
articles.summary: No injuries were reported after two Boeing 737s made contact while taxiing at the airport outside Washington, D.C., during the busy Thanksgiving holiday weekend.

articles.title: Supreme Court Rulings Cheered by Republicans Wound Up Hurting Them
articles.summary: Decisions on voting rights, immigration and corruption generated a backlash that helped spur turnout that drove the Democratic sweep of Congress.

articles.title: Planning Board to Hold Last-Minute Meeting to Consider Trump’s D.C. Construction
articles.summary: President Trump will lose control over the National Capital Planning Commission after Democrats take control of Congress in January. It could give final approval to some of his prized projects.

articles.title: Thanksgiving Storm Outages Ease, but Many on East Coast Remain Without Power
articles.summary: Conditions continued to improve on Friday after heavy rain and strong winds lashed the coast from Virginia to New York. But many remained without power and travel disruptions persisted.

articles.title: After Storms and Power Outages, Some Try Thanksgiving Do-Overs
articles.summary: Some Americans canceled or postponed Thanksgiving dinners amid power outages and storms. They were rescheduled to Friday, Saturday and beyond.

articles.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power a day after US slammed with Thanksgiving storms
articles.summary: Pennsylvania and neighbouring states remained badly affected on Friday after both coasts were lashed with wind and rain.

articles.title: Two American Airlines planes clip wings before takeoff at Reagan airport
articles.summary: No injuries were reported, and the FAA plans to investigate the incident, which occurred during taxiing.

articles.title: Storm Blows Tarp Off Kennedy Center, Exposing Where Trump’s Name Was Removed
articles.summary: High winds dislodged a section of tarp obscuring the removal of the president’s name from the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, whipping up some members of the capital.

articles.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims
articles.summary: The Canadian man, who pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding and abetting suicide earlier this year, said he was remorseful for his actions.

articles.title: Canada : vingt-cinq ans de prison requis contre Kenneth Law pour la vente de « kits de suicide » dans une quarantaine de pays
articles.summary: Ce Canadien de 61 ans trouvait ses victimes sur des forums en ligne d’aide au suicide et leur envoyait du nitrite de sodium, une substance mortelle à forte dose. Il est jugé pour la mort de quatorze personnes au Canada mais il a envoyé des centaines de colis dans le monde entier.

articles.title: California Hiker Falls 500 Feet to His Death While Trying to Help Son
articles.summary: Guillermo Batres, 44, slipped while hiking Mount Baden-Powell, northeast of Los Angeles, earlier this week. Two other hikers who were nearby rescued his teenage son and called 911.

articles.title: Five Big Questions for the 2028 Presidential Race
articles.summary: Will JD Vance and Marco Rubio run? What about Kamala Harris and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez? And, of course, what role will President Trump play?

articles.title: La Cour suprême canadienne consacre la laïcité au Québec dans une décision historique
articles.summary: Cette loi consacre le fait laïc au Québec et tranche avec le multiculturalisme de l’Etat fédéral canadien, ce qui crée des remous dans la classe politique.

articles.title: Marching bands scramble to cover NYC costs after parade rearranged
articles.summary: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

articles.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
articles.summary: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

articles.title: Severe Thanksgiving storms leave roads flooded and trees fallen
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people were without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

articles.title: In Democrats vs. Trump, the Loser May Be Federal Contractors
articles.summary: The incoming Democratic majorities have begun targeting businesses and other outsiders in their planned inquiries, but the president has threatened to fire them if they comply without his permission.

articles.title: Iran : « L’alternative aux bombardements n’est pas nécessairement l’indifférence »
articles.summary: Les frappes américaines ont permis au régime de Téhéran d’affaiblir l’opposition interne, soulignent les économistes Sultan Mehmood et Leonard Wantchekon, dans une tribune au « Monde ». Ils convoquent François Mitterrand et son discours de La Baule, en 1990, pour rappeler que la voie de la négociation reste ouverte.

articles.title: Tempêtes aux Etats-Unis : plus de 900 000 foyers sans électricité sur la Côte est le jour de Thanksgiving
articles.summary: De fortes pluies, du vent violent et des inondations côtières ont affecté l’est du pays en ce jour férié aux Etats-Unis.

articles.title: Au Brésil, Lula nomme un banquier au ministère des finances pour tenter de rassurer les marchés
articles.summary: Luiz Carlos Trabuco prendra ses fonctions après l’investiture, en janvier, du président de gauche, dont la victoire surprise en octobre avait été suivie d’une forte chute de la Bourse et d’une dépréciation du real.

articles.title: La rapporteuse spéciale des Nations unies pour les territoires palestiniens se voit refuser l’entrée au Costa Rica
articles.summary: Francesca Albanese, qui venait recevoir un titre de docteure honoris causa de l’université du Costa Rica, a été interdite d’entrée dans le pays. Elle se trouve sous le coup d’une « alerte internationale pour liens avec des actes terroristes », ont affirmé les services de l’immigration.

articles.title: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
articles.summary: Members of both parties say they want to tackle artificial intelligence policy, but the slow pace of legislating and turf battles could stand in the way.

articles.title: Thanksgiving Is Back on the Menu for Francesca Hong, the Failed Wisconsin Governor Candidate
articles.summary: Francesca Hong, who took heat over a social media post condemning the holiday during her run for the Democratic nomination, now has regrets — and is laughing it all off.
